_comment: Loops that scripts/check-site.py tier 2 flags as rejection sampling but which
have been read and found safe. Keyed on file + enclosing function name rather
than line number, so ordinary edits above the loop do not silently un-allow it.
Every entry needs a reason that says WHY this loop terminates. 'Looks fine' is
not a reason. If you cannot write the terminating argument down, the loop is not
safe -- rewrite it as build-pool / dedupe / shuffle / slice instead.
Adding an entry here is a claim you have checked the worst case, including the
smallest bank or modulus the game can reach. That is the exact step missed when
modular-battle shipped 'while (choices.size < 4)' with a modulus that could be 2.
_roster_exceptions_comment: Games in games/ deliberately absent from .claude/rules/game-roster.md.
The roster is where tier 1 reads each game's levels from, so a game missing from it
is loaded bare and at no ?level= at all. For the entries below that is full coverage,
not a gap -- which is the distinction this list exists to record. If a game you just
added appears here unexpectedly, the fix is the roster, not this file.

roster_exceptions.reason: Unlisted on purpose: the escape-room prototype, never on the portal, with no level tiers to test. A bare load is full coverage. Confirmed by Jon 2026-09-21; canon section 1 records the same 95-directories-to-94-rows gap.

Withdrawn 30 Sep 2026 pending a data rebuild (todo 1.26): index.html is a noindex holding page with no levels to test, the full game is kept as _withdrawn.html. Off the roster until it is rebuilt; a bare load of the holding page is full coverage.

allow.reason: Pads the round to 5 after a deterministic first pass over a shuffled bank. The bank holds far more than 5 distinct re,im keys at every level, so an unused key always remains and the draw cannot starve. Reviewed 2026-09-21.

Cycles a reshuffled pool when the session is longer than the bank. Each pass appends a whole non-empty slice of pool, so questions.length grows by at least one every iteration regardless of what the shuffle returns. Progress is unconditional; only the ordering is random. Reviewed 2026-09-21.

Same cycle-the-bank shape as gradient-hunter. Each pass pushes min(remaining, bank.length) items and bank is non-empty (guarded on the line above), so the loop advances by at least one per pass and cannot spin. Reviewed 2026-09-21.

Pads the option list to 4 by drawing integers from -10..10. That is 21 candidates for 4 distinct slots, so the draw can never exhaust its space and terminates with probability 1 in a handful of passes. Reviewed 2026-09-21.

_tier3_exceptions_comment: Games tier 3 reports as UNSUPPORTED, that have been READ and whose
classification is correct. Tier 3 drives pick-one options and typed answers;
anything else it cannot play, and an unplayable shape is not a defect.
The point of recording them is the diff. Once a game is listed here, a game
NEWLY appearing on the UNSUPPORTED list is a change worth looking at -- it may
mean a game that used to be drivable has stopped taking answers. The run
prints every unrecorded entry for exactly that reason.
As with the loop allowlist above, an entry is a claim you have read the game
and can say what shape it is. Do not bulk-add the list the checker prints:
an unread entry here converts a real signal into a silent one.

tier3_exceptions.reason: Two-phase by design: phase 1 picks the equation from a choice group, phase 2 wants the value TYPED, and some questions add a phase 0 that resolves components first. question_answered does not fire until the typed phase is marked, so a click-only pass never completes a question. Read 2026-09-23.

The answer is BUILT, not picked: #primeBtns offers 2,3,5,7,11,13 and the student presses several to compose a factorisation before submitting. One press is an unfinished answer, not a wrong one, so nothing is marked. Read 2026-09-23.

Stage 1 fills a probability table from a tile bank and is marked by 'Check Table' (checkStage1) only once every blank is filled -- several placements per question. Also the reason its repeated tiles are legitimate: es_gcse_001 ships ['0.25','0.25','0.50','0.10'] because two cells of its table are both 0.25. Read 2026-09-23.

Answer is built, not picked: the student taps each bracket number to open the shared numeric grid, selects a value for it, then presses 'Check Factorisation' -- a click on a grid button is not itself a submitted answer, so question_answered never fires from a single click. Confirmed against the rebuilt game (docs/next-contract-quadratic-factoriser.md, Phase 1, 27 Sep 2026) with a scripted stub-server playthrough driving startEditing/selectNum/checkAnswer directly: every offered session length (8, 16, 24, 174) plays cleanly to game_completed with 100% of clicks marked, so the UNSUPPORTED classification is the driver's generic click-one-option assumption not matching this game's two-step picker, not a defect in the game.

Builds its options as SVG nodes. The driver now dispatches a MouseEvent rather than calling .click() (which SVGElement lacks in Chromium), but the game is a graph-traversal puzzle rather than a question with options, so there is still nothing for a pick-one driver to answer. Read 2026-09-23.

The unlisted escape-room prototype, already a declared roster_exception above. Built to the old 40-minute spec and never on the portal, so it is not a quiz game and has no option group to drive. Read 2026-09-23.
Answers question 1 cleanly and then presents a second phase of the same question that the driver has no move for. The game is fine -- this is the driver's limit. Traced 2026-09-23.
Same shape as spot-the-muppet: #conclusionsGrid is answered and marked, the question advances, and the next stage is not a pick-one group. Traced 2026-09-23.

Not a pick-one/typed-answer game: the student applies a sequence of transform buttons (shift/reflect/stretch) to move a curve, and question_answered fires from checkMatch() comparing the resulting curve to the target, not from any single click being marked. Driven and verified instead by a scripted Playwright pass (curvesMatch, merged-move-counting, and a BFS par check all exercised directly against the shipped page functions) during the 1.25-class fix for defects (a)-(c), 29 Sep 2026.

Cannot start without a named grid: with storage available the student types three initials before Start is enabled, and answers are typed on a keypad (no pick-one group, no <input> to fill). Driven and verified instead by scripts/verify-six-sevens.py (in CI), which creates a grid, plays a full 20-question session through the keyboard against the shipped page, checks every cell, the wrong-answer screen and the returns, and simulates 1,200 sessions against window.SSB. Read 30 Sep 2026.

_b11_form_questions_comment: check-banks.py B11 (options equal in value) skips these. Each is a question whose ask names
the form it tests ("Write in standard form", "Simplify", "Rationalise" ...), so an option
equal in value to another, in a different form, is the point of the question, not a defect.
Keyed on the B11 finding id: the question's content_id (SHA-1 of the whole question) plus the
sorted pair, so moving a question keeps its entry, and editing it orphans the entry, which
fails --ci until someone re-reads the question. 'where' is for a human reader only.
Every entry was read question by question on 2 Oct 2026 (group C of
docs/scan-value-equivalent-options.md, less the 12 questions Jon moved to A or B that day).
Add an entry only with a reason quoting the ask that names the form.

_tier1_phone_overflow_comment: Pages and game starts known to scroll sideways at 320x568 (scripts/check-site.py,
'Tier 1, phone width'). One entry per path and 'at': 'load' is the page as it opens,
'start' is a game after its first level control or Start button. 'width' is the
document width measured when the entry was recorded (web fonts blocked, so in the
fallback font: DejaVu in CI), 'where' the outermost elements past the edge, and
'todo' the docs/todo.md item that owns the fix.
A known overflow passes; an entry that no longer overflows FAILs as stale, so the PR
that fixes a page removes its entry. A game that starts at desktop size but not on a
phone is recorded with "reason": "unreachable" instead of a width.
